To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
muscle-specific microRNAmicroRNAs (miRs) are altered in ALS patients and that the degree of alteration correlates with the severity of the muscle atrophy.
circulating muscle specific microRNAs are useful indicators of muscle differentiation and muscle atrophy in ALS.
the levels of miR-1 and miR-206 are significantly increased in ALS patients and that miR-27 expression is significantly decreased in ALS patients, as compared to controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new biomarkers of ALS, and in particular of the bulbar form, which may be of interest for the early diagnosis and prognosis of ALS.
the identification of biomarkers that could be used in the clinical setting of ALS.
the identification of biomarkers that may help to understand the molecular mechanisms of ALS and to improve the clinical diagnosis of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the muscle mass regulators and microRNAs are involved in ALS pathogenesis, and their expression levels may serve as useful biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis of ALS and for the evaluation of therapeutic efficacy.
circulating miR-206 is a biomarker of muscle differentiation, miR-206/miR-27a ratio is an indicator of muscle atrophy and miR-27 is a biomarker associated with muscle atrophy in ALS.

muscle atrophy in ALS is not a mere consequence of denervation, but rather it is a complex process that includes the activation of a molecular program involving muscle-specific microRNAts, myostatin and its antagonist follistatin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
muscle-specific miR and myostatin/follitstatin ratio could be considered as biomarkers for ALS, especially in bulbar ALS.
the expression of circulating microRNAs is altered in ALS and that these alterations are related to the clinical features of the disease.

muscle atrophy is associated with a significant increase in the levels of miR-133, miR-206 in serum of patients with ALS, which may serve as a biomarker of muscle atrophy and may be useful for monitoring disease progression and therapeutic efficacy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
circulating microRNAs can serve as biomarkers for the diagnosis and prognosis of ALS, and as indicators of therapeutic response.
circulating microRNAs can be useful biomarkers to assess muscle damage and atrophy in patients with ALS.
circulating miRNAs are potential biomarkers for diagnosis and progression of ALS.
